reader.requirement: At --std 85, an elementary item whose effective usage is BINARY, COMPUTATIONAL (COMP) or PACKED-DECIMAL must be refused unless its PICTURE describes a numeric item (only P, S, V and 9). This holds whether the usage is written on the item or inherited from any enclosing group (§1985:VI.5.14.4 GR1), and it refuses alphabetic, alphanumeric, alphanumeric-edited and numeric-edited pictures as well as a missing PICTURE.

edition-consulted.switches: word status of BINARY / COMP / COMPUTATIONAL / PACKED-DECIMAL (all reserved at 85, the same as 2023)

picture-string limits on the same path (MaxStringLength, FoldPictureCase, RepeatableSymbol, the BLANK WHEN ZERO sign arm), none of which decides SR3. The SR3 screen itself (ScreenUsageAgainstPicture) reads no edition

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel|CobolVersion|Edition. over PictureAnalyzer.cs (ScreenUsageAgainstPicture has none) and UsageInheritancePass.cs (none)
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the SR3 screen is edition-free. At 85, a picture-less COMP item with a VALUE literal also draws COBOL0900 for the VALUE-implied PICTURE (a 2002 introduction) in addition to the SR3 refusal; at 2023 it draws the SR3 refusal alone.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses refuse COMP with PIC XX and PACKED-DECIMAL with PIC A(4) (plus a different rule, SR2). Group inheritance, BINARY, edited pictures, mixed alphanumeric pictures, a missing PICTURE and the accepted P/S/V/9 range are not exercised.

probes.printed: 9 x COBOL0881 'requires a PICTURE that describes a numeric item': written BINARY X(4), COMPUTATIONAL A(4), COMP 99X, PACKED-DECIMAL ZZ9, BINARY 9.99, COMP XXBX; inherited BINARY on S1 X(2), PACKED-DECIMAL two levels down on S3 ZZ9, COMP on S4 A. S2 PIC 9(2) under BINARY accepted
probes.expected: every non-numeric picture under BINARY / COMP / PACKED-DECIMAL refused, written or inherited (§1985:VI.5.14.3 SR3, GR1)
S, V, leading P, trailing P, 18 digits and group-inherited PACKED-DECIMAL / BINARY numeric items all accepted and carry their values

probes.printed: P4 PIC S9(18) COMPUTATIONAL VALUE -999999999999999999 displays -999999999999999999
probes.expected: the 85 maximum of 18 digits (§1985:VI.5.9.4 GR3) accepted under COMP

probes.printed: COBOL0881 'a PICTURE clause shall be specified' on N1 COMP, N2 BINARY and inherited N3 PACKED-DECIMAL (the same at --std 2023)
probes.expected: an item with no PICTURE refused (SR3 requires a PICTURE)

probes.printed: 85: COBOL0900 (VALUE-implied PICTURE requires COBOL-2002) and COBOL0881 SR3 on N4 COMP VALUE "AB" and inherited N5; 2023: COBOL0881 SR3 only
probes.expected: a later edition's picture-less VALUE form refused at 85, and SR3 still applied

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.5.14.3 SR3  (5.14.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR3
OK  §1985:VI.5.14.4 GR1  (5.14.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1

reader.notes: ParseUsage maps COMP/COMPUTATIONAL/BINARY to Usage.Binary and PACKED-DECIMAL to Usage.Packed. ScreenUsageAgainstPicture refuses any category but numeric for those usages, and UsageInheritancePass sends inherited usage through the same screen. A small wording point: for a COMPUTATIONAL item the diagnostic says 'USAGE BINARY' because COMP is bound as binary (an implementor choice under GR4). That misnames the clause the programmer wrote but does not affect conformance.

refuter.evidence: rus1 (--std 85 compile-only): COBOL0881 on FILLER PIC X(2) under a COMP group, on a REDEFINES PIC X(2) under a COMP group, on PACKED-DECIMAL +9(3), BINARY 9(3)CR, BINARY *9(3), COMPUTATIONAL 9(3)DB, COMP 99.99, and COMP-3 PIC X(4); BINARY group with subordinate USAGE DISPLAY PIC X(4) refused by COBOL1927 (SR2) so the program is still refused; BINARY-LONG refused COBOL0900 (2002 form, class c). Every SR3 violation tried is refused. Side observation outside this rule: COMP-3 and COMP-5 with numeric pictures are accepted at --std 85 (implementor extensions, not governed by SR3). cite.py: OK §1985:VI.5.14.3 SR3; OK §1985:VI.5.14.4 GR1.
